title: Derived adjunction mates of a short exact sequence of exact functors
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] with unbounded cochain derived categories and localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume K-injective resolutions with injective terms exist; K-injective means that every chain map from an acyclic complex is null-homotopic. Let $E_0=\mathrm{id},E_1,E_2:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ be exact additive functors [def-galois-exact-functor, def-weil-pbc-additive-functor], with specified right adjoints $H_i$ ($H_0=\mathrm{id}$), and a natural objectwise short exact sequence $0\to E_2\xrightarrow{d}E_1\xrightarrow{e}E_0\to0$. Let $P:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ be an additive left adjoint of $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, with a specified class of resolving complexes on which $LP$ is computed by $P$. Assume the total derived functors in what follows exist. All derived adjunctions are those induced from the ordinary adjunctions, normalized on chain maps; shifts have the standard cochain signs.
The ordinary right mates $e^r:H_0\to H_1$ and $d^r:H_1\to H_2$ give, for every injective $I\in\mathcal A$, a split short exact sequence
$$0\to H_0I\xrightarrow{e^r}H_1I\xrightarrow{d^r}H_2I\to0.$$
For a K-injective complex $I$ with injective terms representing $K$, all $H_iI$ are K-injective. The degreewise split sequence
$$0\to FH_0I\to FH_1I\to FH_2I\to0$$
gives a natural distinguished triangle $R_0K\to R_1K\to R_2K\xrightarrow{\delta_K}R_0K[1]$, where $R_i=R(FH_i)$, with its canonical short-exact-sequence boundary. It is independent of the representing resolution under the normalized derived comparisons. The functor $L_i=D(E_i)LP$ is left adjoint to $R_i$. The connecting map in this right triangle is adjoint to the connecting map in the left triangle $L_2M\to L_1M\to L_0M\to L_2M[1]$ induced by $0\to E_2PM\to E_1PM\to E_0PM\to0$ on resolving representatives, with the contravariant cochain Hom sign convention.
Suppose a second system $\mathcal A',\mathcal B',E_i',H_i',P',F',L_i',R_i'$ has these same properties. Let $S:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A')$ and $T:D(\mathcal B)\to D(\mathcal B')$ be exact total left derived functors of additive functors on the abelian categories. Suppose specified natural isomorphisms $\theta_i:L_i'T\xrightarrow{\sim}SL_i$ are induced on resolving complexes by a map of the preceding three-term short-exact-sequence diagrams, allowing quasi-isomorphisms of such diagrams inverted objectwise. In particular this is a comparison of the whole resolution diagrams, not merely their three separate objects. For any $\phi:SK\to K'$ define $\beta_i:TR_iK\to R_i'K'$ as the $L_i'\dashv R_i'$ transpose of
$$L_i'TR_iK\xrightarrow{\theta_i}SL_iR_iK\xrightarrow{S\varepsilon_i}SK\xrightarrow{\phi}K',$$
where $\varepsilon_i$ is the normalized derived counit. Then $\beta_0,\beta_1,\beta_2$ form a morphism from $T$ of the specified right triangle for $K$ to the specified right triangle for $K'$, including
$$\beta_0[1]\circ\delta_{T,K}=\delta_{K'}\circ\beta_2,$$
where $\delta_{T,K}$ includes the canonical shift comparison for $T$. No $\beta_i$ is required to be invertible. The assertion uses the canonical resolution boundaries, not an arbitrary completion of the first two right arrows.

source.place: Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), its functorial cone formula; Tag 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors), with normalization by the chain adjunction; Tag 0A8D (lemma-adjoint-is-exact). The combined adjoint-sequence and comparison assertion is agent-written, using the signed cochain Hom and cone models, not a verbatim Stacks lemma.

proof.text:
Fix an injective object $J$. For every $X$, ordinary adjunction identifies the mate sequence after $\operatorname{Hom}(X,-)$ with
$$0\to\operatorname{Hom}(E_0X,J)\to\operatorname{Hom}(E_1X,J)\to\operatorname{Hom}(E_2X,J)\to0.$$
It is exact: factor a map annihilating $E_2X$ uniquely across the cokernel $E_1X\to E_0X$; extend a map on $E_2X$ across its monomorphism into $E_1X$ by the definition of injectivity. Thus $e^r_J$ is the kernel of $d^r_J$, by precisely this universal factorization for all $X$. Taking $X=H_2J$, surjectivity lifts $1_{H_2J}$ to a section of $d^r_J$. The kernel and this section give $H_1J\cong H_0J\oplus H_2J$ with the stated arrows. No natural choice of splitting is asserted. The right adjoints are additive: for $a,b:J\to J\prime$, the maps induced by $H_i(a+b)$ and by $H_i(a)+H_i(b)$ on $\operatorname{Hom}(X,H_iJ)$ both transpose to postcomposition by $a+b$ on $\operatorname{Hom}(E_iX,J)$. Taking $X=H_iJ$ and evaluating at its identity proves equality; the zero case is identical.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] to $E_i\dashv H_i$: $H_i$ is the right adjoint of the exact $E_i$. Hence every $H_iI$ is K-injective. Step 1 in each degree gives a split short exact sequence of complexes $0\to H_0I\to H_1I\to H_2I\to0$; the mate maps commute with the differential by naturality. Any additive $F$ preserves each splitting, so $Y_i=FH_iI$ form a degreewise split SES. For each additive composite $FH_i$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] applied to its exact homotopy-complex functor $QF H_i$ identifies $QY_i$ with $R_iK$. Additive termwise functors preserve shifts and cones by applying the biproduct matrix defining a cone, so that functor is exact. This computation requires no exactness of $P$ or preservation of K-injectives by $F$.

source.place: Tags 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors) and 070I (lemma-K-injective); signed product Hom: more-algebra.tex Tag 0A5X. The combined argument is agent-written.

proof.text: The SES-triangle lemma gives the distinguished triangle of the $QY_i$, with the canonical SES boundary; the split-triangle formula identifies that boundary with $Q(\pi^{n+1}d_{Y_1}^ns^n)$ for any graded splitting. A morphism between K-injective representatives of $K$ induces a map of all three complexes by $FH_i$, hence a morphism of these particular triangles by SES naturality. Localization is fully faithful on K-injectives; a quasi-isomorphism between them is a homotopy equivalence, preserved by every additive $FH_i$. Therefore these triangle comparisons are invertible, independent of the representing chain map up to homotopy, and compose as the normalized derived comparisons. This proves both naturality in $K$ and independence of its resolution without choosing a triangle completion.

source.place: Tags 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors) and 070I (lemma-K-injective); signed product Hom: more-algebra.tex Tag 0A5X. The combined argument is agent-written.

proof.text:
The ordinary composite adjunction is $E_iP\dashv FH_i$. Its left derived functor is $L_i=D(E_i)LP$: on the stipulated resolving representatives it is $E_iP$, since exact $E_i$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Apply the resolving-derived-adjunction normalization lemma to this composite adjunction and this resolving class. Its right derived pair is $R_i$. This gives $L_i\dashv R_i$, normalized by ordinary transposition of every chain map $E_iPM\to I$. Termwise adjunction also identifies the product Hom complexes
$$\mathsf H(M,FH_iI)\cong\mathsf H(E_iPM,I).$$
Indeed each component is the ordinary additive Hom bijection; naturality in both variables carries $d_I f-(-1)^n f d$ to the same expression on the other side. For resolving $M$, the induced $H^0$ bijection is the derived adjunction, because maps into $I$ are computed up to chain homotopy. The same applies after every shift of $I$.

source.place: Tags 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors) and 070I (lemma-K-injective); signed product Hom: more-algebra.tex Tag 0A5X. The combined argument is agent-written.

proof.text:
Write $b_M:L_0M\to L_2M[1]$ for the canonical boundary of $0\to E_2PM\to E_1PM\to E_0PM\to0$. Apply [lem-sfb-product-hom-ses-boundary] to this left sequence and $I$. It says that the boundary of its reversed product-Hom sequence, on a chain map $f:E_2PM\to I$, is exactly $-Q(f)[1]b_M$. Through the componentwise isomorphisms of step 4, this is the boundary of
$$0\to\mathsf H(M,Y_0)\to\mathsf H(M,Y_1)\to\mathsf H(M,Y_2)\to0.$$
For a cocycle $u:M\to Y_2$, a graded lift is $su$, and its differential, projected to $Y_0$, is $\pi d_{Y_1}su-\pi su d_M=\pi d_{Y_1}su$. By the split-boundary formula of step 3 its localized class is $\delta_K Q(u)$. Consequently, denoting normalized transposition by $\sharp$, for every $u:M\to R_2K$ one has
$$(\delta_Ku)^\sharp=-u^\sharp[1]b_M.\tag{*}$$
Initially $M$ is resolving; its quasi-isomorphic representative and the normalized comparisons extend the identity to every derived $M$. This is the contravariant cochain Hom sign convention in the statement. The two earlier right arrows transpose to precomposition by the corresponding left arrows, directly by ordinary mates and step 4.

source.place: Tags 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors) and 070I (lemma-K-injective); signed product Hom: more-algebra.tex Tag 0A5X. The combined argument is agent-written.

proof.text:
For the second system write $b'_M:L'_0M\to L'_2M[1]$. By hypothesis, for a resolving representative $M$ of $N\in D(\mathcal B)$ and one $M'$ of $TN$, $\theta_i$ is $Q$ of a map $(u_2,u_1,u_0)$ of short exact diagrams from $0\to E'_2P'M'\to E'_1P'M'\to E'_0P'M'\to0$ to the termwise image $0\to sE_2PM\xrightarrow{s(i)}sE_1PM\to sE_0PM\to0$ under the additive functor $s$ underlying $S$, on which $S$ is computed. First, $S(b_N)$ is the canonical boundary $b''$ of this image row: $b_N=-Q(\mathrm{pr})Q(q)^{-1}$ with $q:\operatorname{Cone}(i)\to E_0PM$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; applying $s$ to the cone matrix gives $s\operatorname{Cone}(i)=\operatorname{Cone}(s(i))$ and $s(X[1])=(sX)[1]$ (both differentials are $-s(d)$), carrying $\mathrm{pr},q$ to the projection and the map $q''$ of the image row, a quasi-isomorphism since that row is degreewise exact. As $S$ is computed by $s$ on these complexes and their cone, with the termwise shift comparison, $S(b_N)=-Q(\mathrm{pr})Q(q'')^{-1}=b''$. The third square of the SES-triangle lemma for $(u_2,u_1,u_0)$ now gives
$$\theta_2[1]b'_{TN}=S(b_N)\theta_0\qquad(N\in D(\mathcal B)).\tag{**}$$
For an objectwise quasi-isomorphism of diagrams the squares persist after inverting the three comparisons, isomorphisms under localization; compose along the allowed zigzag. The first two squares give $\theta_i\lambda'_{T(-)}=S(\lambda)\theta_j$ for the left arrows. Naturality and shift compatibility of the $\theta_i$ follow from the same diagram construction and cochain signs. The whole-diagram hypothesis is essential: three unrelated object isomorphisms, or an arbitrary completion of $S$ of the left triangle, would not imply (**).

source.place: Tags 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors) and 070I (lemma-K-injective); signed product Hom: more-algebra.tex Tag 0A5X. The combined argument is agent-written.

proof.text:
Put $N=R_2K$, and let $a_i: L_i'TR_iK\to K'$ denote $\phi\,S(\varepsilon_i)\,\theta_i$, so $a_i=\beta_i^\sharp$. Apply (*) in the primed system, then (**), to obtain
$$(\delta_{K'}\beta_2)^\sharp=-a_2[1]b'_{TN}=-\phi[1]S(\varepsilon_2[1]b_N)\theta_0.$$
Applying (*) in the unprimed system to $1_N$ says
$$\varepsilon_0[1]L_0(\delta_K)=-\varepsilon_2[1]b_N.$$
Substitution changes the previous expression into
$$\phi[1]S(\varepsilon_0[1]L_0(\delta_K))\theta_0.$$
Naturality of $\theta_0$ at $\delta_K$, and the shift compatibility of the normalized adjunctions, identify this last expression with $(\beta_0[1]\delta_{T,K})^\sharp$. Adjunction bijectivity proves the required connecting square. This calculation only composes $\phi$ and the counits; it never inverts a $\beta_i$.

source.place: Tags 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors) and 070I (lemma-K-injective); signed product Hom: more-algebra.tex Tag 0A5X. The combined argument is agent-written.

proof.text:
For either left arrow $\lambda:L_j\to L_i$ ($j,i$ equal to $2,1$ or $1,0$), let $r:R_i\to R_j$ be its right mate and use primes for the other system. Its counit equation is
$$\varepsilon_j L_j(r)=\varepsilon_i\lambda_{R_i}.$$
The first two diagram squares of step 6 say $\theta_i\lambda'_{T(-)}=S(\lambda)\theta_j$. Thus the transpose of $r'\beta_i$ is $a_i\lambda'_{TR_iK}=\phi S(\varepsilon_i\lambda_{R_iK})\theta_j$. Replace the middle composite by $\varepsilon_jL_j(r)$ using the counit equation; naturality of $\theta_j$ makes this the transpose of $\beta_jT(r)$. Hence both earlier squares commute by adjunction bijectivity. Together with step 7 these are exactly the three squares of the claimed morphism of the specified right triangles. All equalities respect the canonical finite sum and shift comparisons already fixed by the resolution diagrams.
